title: News Feed / Timeline Architecture
intro: Design a real-time social timeline system (Twitter/Instagram) generating customized content feeds for hundreds of millions of users.
objectives: Evaluate Fan-Out-On-Write (Push model) vs Fan-Out-On-Read (Pull model).
Architect hybrid models mitigating celebrity 'hotkey' fan-out bottlenecks.
Structure multi-tier Redis timeline caches for sub-10ms feed rendering.
body:
### Fan-Out Models Compared

#### 1. Fan-Out on Write (Push Model)
When user Alice posts a photo, background workers immediately append the post ID into the timeline feed caches of all Alice's followers.
- **Pros**: Reading the feed is lightning-fast ($O(1)$ read from follower's pre-computed Redis list).
- **Cons**: Severe bottleneck for celebrity users with 50M+ followers (one post triggers 50 million write operations).

#### 2. Fan-Out on Read (Pull Model)
Followers fetch posts on demand by querying their followees' latest posts and merging them in memory at read time.
- **Pros**: Zero write amplification on posting.
- **Cons**: Generating the feed is slow ($O(N)$ multi-query merge on every refresh).

### The Industry Hybrid Architecture
- Use **Push (Fan-out on write)** for standard users ($< 25,000$ followers).
- Use **Pull (Fan-out on read)** for celebrities: do not push celebrity posts to follower caches. Instead, merge celebrity posts dynamically into the user's feed upon request.
keyIdea: Use a hybrid fan-out model: push for regular users to keep reads $O(1)$; pull for celebrities to eliminate catastrophic write amplification.

concepts.title: Redis Timeline Lists
concepts.body: Storing the top 800 post IDs in a Redis Sorted Set (ZSET) with timestamp scores delivers instant feed scrolling.

concepts.title: Rank Scoring Engine
concepts.body: Machine learning ranking service scoring candidate post IDs based on engagement probability, affinity, and recency.

examples: Twitter/X timeline architecture transitioning to hybrid fanout.

quiz.prompt: Why does a pure Push (Fan-Out on Write) model fail when a celebrity with 80M followers posts a tweet?
options: A single write generates 80 million concurrent cache writes, causing massive queue lag and worker thread starvation
Redis cannot store more than 10,000 items
quiz.explanation: The extreme write amplification of 80M writes per post overwhelms message queues and background worker pools.
